newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Core business boosts Anglian Water H1.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Core business boosts Anglian Water H1.

text.p: British utility Anglian Water Plc reported on Tuesday a near six-percent increase in first-half pre-tax profits and said it plans to invest more to improve customers' water supplies.

The southeast England company's pre-tax profits rose to 132.7 million pounds ($219 million) for the half-year ended September 30, up from 125.8 million pounds a year-ago with help from strong results at its core regulated business.
Anglian also raised its interim dividend to 10.2 pence per share from 8.9 pence in the prior half-year.
In addition, the company said it planned to invest 34 million pounds to enable the transfer of surplus water to possible areas of scarcity next summer if winter rainfall is lower than average.
"Most years I guess we would spend about five million a year," managing director Alan Smith said.
The additional investment will be included in the company's capital spending budget of about 340 million pounds this year versus 284 million last year, he said.

Anglian's results were in line with analysts' estimates ranging from 123.0-140.0 million pounds but failed to lift Anglian's shares, which drifted 11.5-pence lower to 547.5 by 1130 GMT amid overall weakness in the British stock market.
"We are hopeful that the full-year performance will be as good, if not a bit better, than the half-year, but we've still got another six months to go," Smith told Reuters.
Operating profits for Anglian's regulated business rose 11.8 percent to 171.6 million pounds in the first half compared to 153.5 million in the year-earlier period.
"The regulated business has turned in an excellent half-year performance," Anglian said in a statement.
But its said non-regulated businesses had raised operating losses, mainly due to planned increases in marketing costs.

Operating losses for Anglian's ongoing process engineering and products businesses narrowed to 3.7 million pounds for the half year from 3.8 million pounds, but the company said the recovery was slower-than-expected.
"We would hope that they would get into profit in the second six months so hopefully, the year-end result won't be quite as bad as the half-year result," Smith said.
Meanwhile, marketing costs for bids in countries such as Chile and the Philippines rose to 2.8 million pounds vs 700,000.

"That's exactly in line with what we said we were going to do," Smith said, noting that the company previously decided to raise its marketing expenses for contracts to about six million pounds per year. ($1=.6051 Pound)
